next_authority.question: For the actual C5I prescribed-head state pairs, how do current K_cell, arithmetic center-boundary K, and a theory-derived nonlinear half-cell conductivity/flux representation compare before any new dynamic Reference formulation is considered?

scientific_interpretation: The persistent high-resolution discrepancy is strongly sensitive to prescribed-head boundary discretization while HOLD remains exactly unchanged in every counterfactual.

The distance-semantic control has the larger main-effect norm: about 0.01936 cm/d, approximately 83 percent of the current spatial-gap RMSE. However, doubling the center-to-boundary distance worsens the R512-R1024 gap from about 0.02340 to 0.03072 cm/d, so C5J does not support replacing the physical half-cell distance.

Extending swkmean=1 arithmetic conductivity averaging to the prescribed boundary has a smaller main-effect norm of about 0.00679 cm/d and reduces the spatial gap only modestly, to about 0.02279 cm/d or 97.4 percent of current.

The combined counterfactual worsens the gap to about 0.03044 cm/d. The factorial interaction norm is about 0.00583 cm/d, around 30 percent of the larger main-effect norm, so geometry and conductivity localization are not separable as purely additive effects.
A smaller inter-grid gap is not continuum truth. None of the three counterfactuals is admitted as a new Reference discretization.

The next question is mathematical rather than empirical tuning: what local nonlinear half-cell flux is implied by the Richards/Darcy operator and the B14 constitutive law for the actual prescribed-head state pairs?
